title: The Cell Cycle
short: A cell spends most of its life in interphase (G1 growth, S DNA copying, G2 preparation), then divides in the mitotic phase. Checkpoints decide whether it goes on.
trouble: Students think interphase is a resting phase. The cell is busy growing and copying its DNA; it is only "resting" from division.

blocks.html: You started as one cell. You now have trillions, and many of them are still dividing to grow and to replace worn-out cells. Each of those cells follows the same repeating program, the cell cycle, built around the chromosomes it must copy and share out.

A cell spends most of its life in interphase: G1 (growth), S (DNA synthesis: copying the chromosomes) and G2 (more growth and preparation). Then it divides in the mitotic (M) phase: mitosis and cytokinesis. Checkpoints decide whether it goes on.

blocks.name: bi-chart

opts.title: A typical 24-hour cycle of a dividing human cell

blocks.cap: Approximate times for a dividing human cell in culture. Mitosis is only about an hour; interphase is the rest.

items: G1: the cell grows, makes proteins and organelles, and does its normal job.
S: every chromosome is copied, so each becomes two sister chromatids.
G2: the cell grows more, makes the proteins needed for division, and checks the copied DNA.
M: mitosis divides the nucleus; cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm.
G0: many cells, such as most nerve cells, leave the cycle and stop dividing, sometimes for good.

blocks.html: Interphase is when a cell does its real work, and it is also the preparation for division: a cell must double its DNA and roughly double its contents before it can split into two complete cells. Because each phase takes a fixed share of the cycle, you can estimate how long each lasts by counting. In a slide of dividing cells, the fraction of cells in a phase is about the fraction of time the cycle spends in it.

blocks.title: Time from a count
blocks.q: In an onion root tip, 180 of 200 cells are in interphase and 20 are in mitosis. If the whole cycle takes 24 hours, about how long is mitosis?

blocks.title: Before and after S
blocks.q: A cell with $2n = 6$ goes from G1 through S into G2. What happens to its chromosomes and chromatids?
steps: In G1: 6 chromosomes, each a single chromatid: 6 chromatids.
In G2: still 6 chromosomes (6 centromeres), now 12 chromatids.
blocks.a: 6 chromosomes throughout; chromatids go from 6 to 12.

blocks.html: Thinking interphase is a resting phase. The cell is busy growing, working and copying its DNA. It is only "resting" from division, and the S phase in the middle of it is one of the most important steps of the whole cycle.
